evidence: Walked all 52 criteria (gates: render 1, constraints 2; functional 43; polish 6 binary; visual 3 likert). Every functional/gate/polish criterion names a concrete browser-observable bar with readback (rendered editor lines, line/column readout, console text, preview text, library entries, revision lists, disabled state, computed styles or screenshots), judge-chosen distinctive fixtures/markers (unique titles, markers built from halves in cw_dynamic_code_refused, hostile marker in cw_preview_isolation), and durable evidence where state matters (storage clear + reload in cw_shared_saved_record; restart_app + fresh page in cw_save_reload_restart; fresh third page in cw_stale_save_refused/keeps_draft; freshly loaded page revision count in cw_restore_request_repeat_safe and cw_history_restore_adds_revision). Negative legs carry positive controls. No criterion grades a source read or a response shape without state change; constraints cw_custom_document_surface is a read-only live-DOM fact check, which is browser-decidable. Visual likert rows are craft judgments with anchors (check 41 known false positive, not a #32 defect). Focus on the new bullet tests/app_context.md:21: 'A modifier-click means the modifier key is held down during the click. With the click tool, pass the modifier in its modifiers option; in the code runner, use page.keyboard.down for the modifier, page.mouse.click at the character position, then page.keyboard.up. Pressing and releasing the modifier before an ordinary click is not a modifier-click... count the visible carets after each click before typing.' Verified against the pinned tool: @playwright/mcp@0.0.79 core tools include browser_click with `modifiers` (array) and browser_run_code_unsafe (core, not behind --caps); coordinate tools (browser_mouse_click_xy) are behind --caps=vision, which judge.toml args do not pass, so the code-runner route the bullet names is the correct position-precise path. Playwright applies held keyboard modifiers to subsequent mouse events, and the golden reads event.altKey/ctrlKey/metaKey on mousedown (custom-editor.js:364) and renders each caret as a visible span.caret/.multi-caret (custom-editor.js:1221), so the three multi-caret criteria (cw_multi_caret_typing_atomic, cw_multi_caret_delete, cw_same_line_carets) are decidable by real input with source readback. The bullet adds no requirement (ui.md:9 already asks for both Alt+Click and Ctrl/Cmd+Click), stays within the allowed real-input exception (app_context.md:20), and is consistent with functional prompt.md:22. Plausible broken app (adds carets on plain clicks or ignores modifiers) fails via 'one ordinary click' + 'nowhere else'/'either modifier-click does not add a caret'; conforming alternative using pointerdown/getModifierState still sees the held modifier, so it is not falsely failed. Minor wording observation (P3, not a defect): with browser_click the target is a snapshot ref/selector clicked at its centre, so 'aim at the character position' is only achievable through the code runner unless the app exposes a per-character element; the bullet's own centre warning makes this clear enough. Risk=true because the only runtime evidence cited (hosted Oracle run losing the three multi-caret criteria) predates this bullet, the raw-evidence-index.json named in the assignment does not exist, and no configured judge run on this candidate shows the judge now carrying the modifier; the fix is source- and tool-schema-verified only.
